items.title: scikit-learn version 1.9 highlights: GPU acceleration with the Python array API standard
items.author: Probabl
items.content:
<article>In this installment of our series on version 1.9, scikit-learn contributor Emily Chen explains how you can accelerate your scikit-learn workflows on GPUs.

For the past decade, scikit-learn has delegated computations to core dependencies like NumPy, SciPy, and Cython. All three were designed for CPUs, which meant that scikit-learn workflows were limited to CPUs, too. 

For  data science teams with access to GPUs, that design has become a bottleneck. GPU support promised significant speed-ups. But until recently, supporting GPUs meant writing a separate code path for every array library: one for NumPy, one for CuPy, another for PyTorch. For a project of scikit-learn's size, that meant fragmented code, a heavy maintenance burden, and a form of vendor lock-in that its maintainers were not willing to accept. 
 
💡The Python array API standard offers a solution. It is a shared specification for NumPy-like operations, adopted by the major array libraries. By writing to the standard rather than to a specific library, scikit-learn stays backend agnostic. Developers from Probabl, Quansight, NVIDIA, and the wider scientific community have been heads-down making GPU support an option in scikit-learn.</article>
